On Your Mark (1995) is proof that a seven-minute film can leave a lasting mark on animation history. Directed by Hayao Miyazaki as a music video for the Japanese duo Chage & Aska, the short became an important creative milestone for Studio Ghibli.

Miyazaki created the project while taking a break during the development of Princess Mononoke, using it as a chance to experiment with new ideas. It also marked one of Studio Ghibli’s earliest uses of computer-generated animation, blending digital techniques with the studio’s signature hand-drawn style.

Many of the ideas and techniques explored in On Your Mark were later refined for Princess Mononoke, making the short far more significant than its runtime suggests. Nearly three decades later, it remains one of Miyazaki’s most inventive and visually ambitious works.
